q: What does a Media In node read?
a: A Media In node brings in a picture from the project (a clip, a sequence, another comp) or from a track under the comp clip. Each node takes pictures in on the left, does one job and passes a picture out on the right; the comp shows what reaches its Media Out node, which every new comp starts with. Solid is a flat colour and Gradient a linear or radial blend of two colours, e.g. as a background.

q: How do I add a node to a comp?
a: Open Window ▸ Compositor (or the Compositing workspace; the Fusion page in the Resolve workflow). With no comp clip selected it offers New Comp Clip (`comp.newClip`): a comp the size of the sequence on V1 at the playhead. Right-click the empty canvas to add a node (`comp.addNode`), drag from an output dot to an input dot to connect, select a node and press Delete to remove it. Moving a node on the canvas doesn't change the picture.

q: Where are a comp node's settings?
a: Click one node: its settings appear as rows under the canvas, like Effect Controls rows (numbers you drag or type, swatches, menus); each change is one undo step. A Text node shows the title's controls: type in its text field and the title changes as you type. Selecting several nodes hides the rows.

q: How do I list everything in a comp from a script?
a: `comp.get` lists the comp's nodes, connections, output node, size, frame rate and length, the run order and, if it can't run, why. `comp.setSource` with `node` and either `item` (a project item) or `track` (the clip under the comp on that track), plus an optional `offset`, sets what a Media In reads. These are commands only for now.

q: How do I get back to the finished comp picture after viewing a node?
a: Double-click a node (or right-click ▸ View, or pick it in the Show menu at the top right of the canvas) to show its output in the Program monitor at the comp's size. Pick Show: Media Out (or send `comp.view` with no node) to go back to the finished picture. Viewing changes only the monitor, not the comp.

q: What does comp.explain return?
a: `comp.explain` (control channel or MCP) reads the graph and returns a `summary` (how many nodes build the picture from how many sources), `lines` describing each node in flow order with its own name and changed settings, and `unused` nodes that don't reach Media Out. Add `time` in ticks to describe animated settings at that moment. It only describes what's in the graph.

q: What do Mask Feather and Mask Expansion do in a comp?
a: One Mask node holds up to sixteen shapes (Add ellipse / Add rectangle). Under each shape Mask Feather softens the edge, Mask Opacity fades the shape and Mask Expansion grows or shrinks it; Inverted keeps the outside; Delete removes it. On a keyframed shape a change is a keyframe at the playhead. Each click is one undo step.

q: and how do I reshape it?
a: Keep the Mask node selected and work on the Program monitor: drag a square point to move it, drag inside the shape to move all of it, drag a Bézier handle to bend the curve (Alt for one handle alone), Alt-click a point to switch smooth / corner, Ctrl-click an edge to add a point or a point to delete it.

q: What does Convert to Comp Clip build inside the comp?
a: Each clip becomes a Media In followed by a Transform holding its Motion settings, laid over each other bottom track first by Merge nodes holding their Opacity and blend mode, so the frame looks the same. The comp clip replaces them on the lowest of their tracks. Edit ▸ Undo brings the clips back.

q: Is there a ready-made batch that builds example comps?
a: Yes: `tools/comp-accept.json` in the repository is a command batch an agent or script runs through the control channel's `command_batch`; it puts a keyed-subject comp on V2 and a title-over-footage comp on V3, both reading the footage on V1.

q: Does the compositor use the GPU?
a: Comps are drawn on the graphics card at the size they appear; a Media In reading a track under the comp clip takes frames straight from the decoder, so 1080p comps and 4K comps at half resolution play in real time (measured on synthetic footage). These fall back to the processor: a comp clip with its own effects, grade or opacity masks; a Media In reading a project clip rather than a track (for now); a comp too large for the card or needing over 2 GB; settings the card can't run.

q: Which keyers does Revolution have?
a: Three keyers in Effects ▸ Video Effects ▸ Keying: Ultra Key keys one colour by hue and saturation (green / blue screens; the most controls, needs an even screen); Color Key keys one colour by distance (flat graphic colours, quick tests; hard edge, no spill or cleanup); Luma Key keys dark or bright areas (a logo on black, a sky; dark clothes go too).

a: Revolution's keyers are effects on the clip, like Premiere's: Ultra Key, Color Key and Luma Key with the same names and controls. In a comp, a Key node uses Ultra Key or Luma Key. Resolve keys in Color page nodes or Fusion's Delta Keyer instead.

q: Which track does the green screen clip go on?
a: Put the background on Video 1 and the green-screen clip on Video 2 above it; apply Ultra Key to the green-screen clip (`effects.apply` with `ultra_key`). Set Key Color with the eyedropper on mid-green, then pick Setting: Default first, Relaxed if edges look chewed, Aggressive if green is left; Custom uses the sliders as you set them. Fix the key colour first: everything later works on its result.

q: What does Ultra Key's Color Channel output show?
a: With Output ▸ Alpha Channel the matte shows in black and white: grey speckles in the background → raise Tolerance or Transparency (Setting: Custom) or light the screen more evenly; holes in the person → lower Tolerance or raise Pedestal; jagged edges → Soften. Color Channel shows the foreground colours with spill removed but nothing keyed, to judge spill alone. Set Output back to Composite.

q: What does Choke do on a key?
a: Choke shrinks the matte inwards (5–20 usually; large values eat hair); Soften feathers the edge; Contrast and Mid Point make the matte's greys harder around the mid point; Spill removes the green cast, with Desaturate, Range and Luma for strength, colours and brightness; Color Correction fits the foreground to the new background. A common order is key colour, setting, matte check, choke / soften, spill, colour correction, but going back is normal.

q: What do Cutoff and Threshold do in Luma Key?
a: Luma Key: Cutoff is the brightness at and below which a pixel is fully gone, Threshold the brightness at and above which it's fully kept, fading between (white logo on black: Cutoff ≈ 10, Threshold ≈ 30). Color Key: Key Color with the eyedropper, Color Tolerance for how far from it still goes, Edge Feather to soften. Edge Thin does nothing yet.

q: What can follow a track in Revolution?
a: It looks for small detailed spots (corners, texture, text) inside the area you mark and follows them frame to frame, writing keyframes; flat areas have nothing to follow and it stops with lost track. Three things can follow: a mask (`masks.track`, Mask Path's track buttons), a layer's Motion (`tracking.attach`, Attach to Track), or Corner Pin's four points (`tracking.cornerPin`, Track Surface).

q: What area does Attach to Track follow?
a: Attach to Track follows the detail in a 120 × 120 pixel box around the layer's Position, in the shot below. Click ▶▶ or ◀◀ (single arrows do one frame); each run is one undo step, and clicking again stops it.

q: Why does Corner Pin tracking keep corners on even when they leave frame?
a: A flat surface at an angle changes shape predictably (perspective). Revolution follows the detail inside the four corners, works out that shape change each frame and moves the points with it, so corners stay on even when they leave the frame or something passes in front. It tracks the clip right below the one with Corner Pin (or the clip itself); scripts can pick another with `source`.

q: In Premiere I'd keyframe Corner Pin by hand or use Mocha. What's the Revolution way?
a: Apply Corner Pin (Effects ▸ Video Effects ▸ Distort) to the replacement picture, set its four corners on a clear frame, then click Track Surface ▶▶ / ◀◀: the tracker moves the corners with the surface. It runs in the background, shows in the jobs list, and keeps what it tracked if stopped.
